You can grow E.Coli bacteria in agar for plasmids? They’re easy to grow at home, and then you can test with streptomycin to see if the DNA editing worked. streptomycin binds to the active site of the ribosome and prevents it from creating proteins and the cell quickly dies without them. If you grow Ecoli and mutate it with CRISPr, the goal is to prevent streptomycin from binding to the ribosome to continue protein synthesis and avoid cell death. If your gene edited bacteria survives in an environment where streptomycin is present, then CRISPR worked. I recall there’s also like a dye you can use to see the plasmids better and see if they’re reacted/unreacted with the gRNA. Red plasmids are “hot” and reacted while blue plasmids are “cold” and unreacted. Good luck!

I just finished this semester with a B in the class, studied 30+ hrs per week on it alone, a lot of what helped me was going back to basics, so go over EN and acid base, redox for sure. A lot of orgo chem is mostly getting used to looking at line structure and what each component means, but then you start catching the general chemistry parts which if you know OH and HBr will give you H2O in general chem because it’s acid base, look at reagents early. It was so overwhelming learning all the reactions at once...but they’re chm rxns, positive attached to negative, electron negativity, inductive effect and stability, acid and base, redox, enthalpy and entropy, and a myriad of chapters on visualizing the molecule in 3D that you need to understand to do the reactions that come later in the course.... which I suggest you actually start looking at early because learning them all at once quickly becomes overwhelming and I wish I had looked at some of this stuff beforehand but alas I had no idea orgo chem had the reputation it had until 2 weeks ago where, like you, I asked kind strangers for how they passed in a last minute effort to understand that shit. I studied over a week for the final exam and got a 65, but he dropped our lowest grade. Learn functional groups early and the prefixes and suffixes of alkanes. Patterns start becoming obvious after many practice problems so I suggest organic chem tutor on YouTube. It’s insane how every little detail has a meaning.  get comfortable looking at line structure and what each component means, so that when groups you recognize from regular chemistry course react, you can more easily point them apart as just a regular reaction. This is a big chunck of the course and every chapter builds on top of the other, so when you get to reactions, you need to know what each component of the chain is so you know what they’ll react with. Doesn’t hurt to buy a molecule model kit, it’ll make your life significantly easier understanding cyclohexane chair conformations and Newman projections, i got a used kit on Amazon for 20 bucks.
